newsitem.title: USA: Minn. Fed's Stern says economy expansion continues.
newsitem.headline: Minn. Fed's Stern says economy expansion continues.

text.p: The U.S. economy is growing at a steady pace, showing little evidence the seven-year old expansion is phasing out, said the president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis Gary Stern.
"Prospects seem excellent for this positive (economic) performance to continue through the balance of this year and into the next," Stern told an audience here.
"Evidence that the economy might somehow run out of steam is lacking. Indeed, there are few, if any, hints of serious trouble spots at the moment," Stern added.
The Minneapolis Fed chief said the U.S. economy appears well-positioned for another year or more of balanced growth.
Stern also said the ultimate goal of the Federal Reserve monetary policy is to provide sustained economic growth.

"Let me emphasize that our commitment to low inflation, significant as it is, is not the ultimate goal of (monetary) policy. Our ultimate goal is sustained growth and rising standards of living over time," Stern said.
Shortly after the speech, Stern told reporters here that he did not share other economists' concerns about incipient rises in wages.
"While there's clearly signs of some acceleration in wages, if you look at (overall labor) compensation more broadly it's not so obvious," Stern said.
He also said he was not "terribly concerned" about others' worries over burgeoning consumer debt.
